title: CLAUDE.md says the path-filter blast radius is unenumerated; it has been enumerated, and the condition is a CONJUNCTION rather than the path filter alone
description: QCLI-359 landed a sentence saying which other fleet repos have path-filtered required workflows is UNENUMERATED by either us or opum-agent. That was true when written and is now false: opum-agent swept it (their OPAG record, opum-ai/opum-agent#834, 2026-09-20T15:00:56Z) and this session re-ran it independently rather than relaying it. Both sweeps read the same objects - 10 repos, 22 workflow files, 32 required contexts, quest-web skipped for having no required contexts on either ref - and quest-cli is the only affected repository. This sessions detector additionally flagged lore-cli Tracker integrity, which is a FALSE POSITIVE: it matched paths-ignore at file scope without checking which trigger carries it. In lore-cli ci.yml the filter is on push only, push is branches [main] only, and pull_request is deliberately left unfiltered with a comment saying why - so the required status check can never be skipped into a permanent pending that deadlocks a PR. Verifying the extra finding rather than reporting it produced the sharper result: quest-cli and lore-cli have the SAME workflow shape (paths on push, pull_request unfiltered), so the path filter alone is not the condition. The condition is a conjunction of that filter with a gate on main satisfied by fast-forward push, which requires the contexts green on a SHA that can predate any PR. lore-cli gates dev, where every landing is through a PR and the unfiltered trigger always supplies the row; its main carries no ruleset at all.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The UNENUMERATED sentence is replaced by the enumeration result, dated, attributed to opum-agent, and marked as independently re-measured here rather than relayed

The profile states the condition as the conjunction (path-filtered push trigger AND a main gate satisfied by fast-forward push), not as the path filter alone, and names lore-cli as the repo with the same workflow shape and no exposure
The false positive is recorded with its cause (matching the filter at file scope without checking trigger attachment), since it is what produced the conjunction framing
The dev-gating count is corrected from the hedged at least one to the three measured here, without implying this session swept anything it did not

implementationNotes: Sweep method and its limits, since the clean half of the result is only as good as what it read. Structural: reads rules/branches/{main,dev} for required contexts, then every workflow file in each repo, and flags a required context whose workflow carries a paths/paths-ignore key. Deliberately NOT empirical - reading which contexts sit on todays dev HEAD measures that commits paths rather than the configuration, so a filter that happens to match todays commit reads clean and is not. Guards, because a clean answer here authorises leaving the profile alone: the run fails rather than passes if it read fewer than 10 repos, if any API call errored, or if it found zero findings fleet-wide - the last one because quest-cli is a known instance, so a zero result means the detector is broken, not that the fleet is clean. Its positive control is rediscovering quest-cli from configuration, the opposite direction from how the instance was originally found (an observed missing check-run). Known weakness, which is the one that fired: it matches the filter key at file scope and does not check which trigger carries it, so it cannot distinguish a push-only filter from one that also covers pull_request. That is exactly the lore-cli false positive, and the conjunction framing came out of running it down.
finalSummary: Replaced the UNENUMERATED sentence QCLI-359 left in CLAUDE.md with the enumeration result, and corrected the dev-gating count from a hedged "at least one" to the three measured (lore-cli, lore-web, opum-fleet). opum-agent swept the fleet and this session re-ran it independently rather than relaying the number; both read 10 repos, 22 workflow files, 32 required contexts, quest-web skipped, and quest-cli is the only affected repository. The independent run also produced a false positive on lore-cli Tracker integrity by matching paths-ignore at file scope without checking trigger attachment; reading the file withdrew it (filter on push only, push restricted to main, pull_request deliberately unfiltered with a comment giving the deadlock reason). Running that down rather than reporting it is what produced the substantive correction: quest-cli and lore-cli share the same workflow shape, so the path filter alone is not the condition - it is that filter AND a gate on main satisfied by fast-forward push, which is what requires green contexts on a SHA that can predate any PR. A sibling adopting this repos promotion shape acquires the exposure without editing any workflow, which a filter-only check cannot see. Verified: quest agents --check exit 0 (managed block untouched), lore check exit 0 across 63 files, sweep exit 0 with its read-count and positive-control guards satisfied.
